declared.note: This file must be committed before any hardware run. Its value is its timestamp: pinned after the fact it proves nothing.

expected_at_threshold.note: (Q,Q) is deterministic at every gamma -- the outcome is always CC, so on a noiseless device all shot noise comes from the (dev,Q) arm.

expected_device_bias.direction: no direction is predicted. See amendment 1: the original one-directional claim rested on a mechanism that does not hold, so the pass criterion is symmetric.
expected_device_bias.mechanism: a depolarizing channel maps BOTH arms by the same affine rule, p -> (1-q)p + q*uniform, so the gain becomes (1-q)*gain_ideal. A positive rescaling cannot move a zero crossing. The earlier claim that the falling (dev,Q) curve is dragged down faster than the flat (Q,Q) curve is wrong: both are pulled toward 2.25 in the same proportion.

simulation_scope.note: each channel is applied uniformly to an idealised two-qubit circuit with ideal one-qubit gates. A real device can bias the crossing by MORE than any figure here, in either direction.
omits: gates introduced by transpilation to a native basis
simulation_scope.purpose: rule out the mechanism the original registration invoked; nothing more

superseded_table.note: attributed to simulation at 200k shots per point, but no code produced them and no channel tried here reproduces them; they are 5x to 100x larger than any simulated bias.

pass_criterion.decision_rule: PASS if and only if |measured - 0.684719203| <= 0.026573 rad. FAIL otherwise, in either direction, including when no sign change is found in the swept range. There is no separate 'materially above' clause: amendment 1 removed the one-directional bias claim that would have justified an asymmetric rule.
pass_criterion.rationale: shot noise alone is NOT the whole error budget: a real device biases the crossing downward by an amount comparable to the 3-sigma shot tolerance. Pre-registering shot noise only would have set a criterion the hardware fails for reasons unrelated to whether the EWL threshold is correct. Both terms are fixed here, in advance, and neither may be widened after the run.
pass_criterion.systematic_support: registered before the run; not derived from the illustrative channels, which do not bound device error

deviation_strategy.why: at gamma=pi/2 the best reply to Q is Q, so an argmax taken there returns Q and the deviation gain is identically zero

protocol_fixed_in_advance.estimator: last sign change of (payoff(dev,Q) - payoff(Q,Q)), linearly interpolated between adjacent grid points

execution_stack_frozen.eligibility_error_is: the two-qubit gate error of the SELECTED PAIR, not the device median
execution_stack_frozen.initial_layout: fixed before submission to the lowest-two-qubit-error connected pair in the calibration snapshot, recorded as explicit physical qubit indices
